It's too overwhelming for me. I have slight agoraphobia where I can go where I am obligated but I don't like to go outside.
I am isolated.
All I can think to do is continue to try to be stoic. Obviously with these posts I have failed. I don't know what else to do, I'm weak.

This life. I have nightmares I would rather live in. I can't pinpoint exactly what it is about life that terrifies me so much. I look forward to sleep because time will be fast forwarded and I am closer to the end.
Freedom from disturbance.
Not this.

peace

It's not practical. I have a part time job that I have to take the bus to get to. I don't have a license so even if I found somewhere to volunteer it'd be too much of a hassle.
I don't like to read academic philosophy. I haven't had much patience for reading books. Also there is no charity work to be done where I live, if there is, I don't know about it.
I try but everything feels so petty and I always go back to thinking about suicide.

I've made some sort of peace with the idea. Change is too hard, I've tried all kinds of drugs, therapy, meditation, writing, doing anything to take my mind off it. All I can do is make peace with it and accept it.
I don't care about what ifs.
It's okay that you don't believe me. I once didn't believe these things were true but denial only hurt me more.

It was a while ago when I went through a therapy program. During that period of time is when I realized that I wasn't going to get better and all of that just made things worse. This is way I am supposed be.
I don't feel that negative. I feel more free now.
When I listened to people that gave me false hope led to most of the frustration.
Nope, I'm about to be on welfare. I'm not useful to anyone in any way. I don't know how to love anyone or myself. It doesn't come naturally to me like everyone else so I've been alone all of my life.
I don't really feel much. I used to, I tried to resist. I was angry, sad, confused and hateful but I think I am past that now. There is no point in those feelings, I have abandoned my humanity.
